value: tools/capture.py (2026-11-25) takes shots of the demo app for a caller outside this repo; seabear.toml at the root names it. `list` prints the shots as JSON; `shoot --out <folder> [--appearance light|dark] [--set KEY=VALUE] <shot> ...` writes <name>-<appearance>.png and a capture.json beside them (how each was posed, its size, the simulator, the library's version and commit); `record` is taken and stops, since no pose plays on its own. THE SHOTS ARE READ FROM THE HARNESS: the cases of `enum Snapshot` in Sources/Demo/SnapHarness.swift, up to its `static let current` line, so a pose added there can be asked for with nothing changed in the script. Renaming the enum or moving that line breaks the read, and the script stops with a plain message. The version in capture.json is `SeaBearKit.version`, read from Sources/SeaBearKit/SeaBearKit.swift and written into the bundle's Info.plist. BY DEFAULT IT CREATES ITS OWN SIMULATOR (an iPhone 17 Pro on the newest iOS, named 'SeaBearKit capture') and builds the library and the demo into a scratch folder with swiftc, the same steps as shoot.sh ([[commands.screenshots]]), then deletes both, so nothing lands in .build. SEABEAR_SIM / SEABEAR_APP name a simulator and a built SeaBearKitDemo.app to use instead. THE APPEARANCE IS THE CALLER'S for every shot: `dark` (the menu in midnight) is meant for --appearance dark and comes out washed in light. THE POSE CHECK: a launch that came up without SEABEAR_SNAP would show the menu in sunset, the same picture as the `menu` shot (DemoApp falls back to .sunset and pushes nothing). So after each shot the script reads the process's environment from the Mac (`ps eww -p <pid>`: a simulator's app is a host process) and launches again, up to three times, when the variable is missing, and it waits for the last process to be gone before each launch. shoot.sh has no such check. Seven shots take about 80 seconds. CHECKED 2026-11-25 on Xcode 27.2: all seven in light, `dark` and `menu` in dark, each looked at; no launch came up without its pose in those runs. Separate from shoot.sh, which still makes the marketing set on the Pro Max.
